caption: Average performance of different models on the November 2024 AMC-10 and AMC-12 tests. This is the average score (with maximum score 150) over the four tests on 100 runs with temperature t=0.5. We chose t = 0.5 to follow simple-evals <cit.>. Error bars are 2 of the estimate. On competition math, scores well above its weight-class even compared to non–open-weight models.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average performance of various large and small language models on the November 2024 AMC-10 and AMC-12 tests, with scores normalized to a maximum of 150. The horizontal axis lists the models in the following order: Llama-3-3 70B, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Qwen 2.5 14B-Instruct, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Qwen 2.5 72B-Instruct, Gemini Flash 1.5, Gemini Pro 1.5, and phi-4. The vertical axis represents the average score, ranging from 60 to 90, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each model is represented by two adjacent bars: a light blue bar for the "Large model" and a dark blue bar for the "Small model," as indicated in the legend. The light blue bars correspond to larger models, while the dark blue bars correspond to smaller models. The chart shows that phi-4, the smallest model, achieves the highest average score of 91.8, followed by Gemini Pro 1.5 at 89.8. Other models show varying performances: Llama-3-3 70B scores 66.4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet scores 74.8, Qwen 2.5 14B-Instruct scores 77.4, GPT-4o scores 77.9, GPT-4o mini scores 78.2, Qwen 2.5 72B-Instruct scores 78.7, and Gemini Flash 1.5 scores 81.6. Each bar is accompanied by error bars representing ±2 standard errors of the estimate, based on 100 runs with a temperature setting of t=0.5. The models are sorted left to right in a non-alphabetical, seemingly performance-based order, with phi-4 placed last and achieving the highest score. The chart visually emphasizes that phi-4 outperforms larger models, including non-open-weight ones, in competition math tasks.
